messages.author: 10c22402db922db9
messages.subject: nested random effect
parts:
Hello INLA people!

 

I have quite a simple problem which involves a binomial regression with a random walk. I have data for several regions and for several years. I am interested to model it thusly:

y ~ 0 + region + f(year, model = “rw2”, etc)

But I would like to nest the random effect within region, is that possible? The analogue mixed effect model (without random walk) would be something like this:

y ~ 0 + region + (1|year:region)

I have been struggling to find a syntax within f() that does this.

 

Kind regards,

 

Christoph

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] nested random effect
parts:
If by nesting you mean having a separate rw2 for each region, but with
the same parameter for all of them, something like this should do it:

f(year, model="rw2", group=region, control.group=list(model="iid")

Finn

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: nested random effect
parts:
On Fri, 2014-04-25 at 06:59 -0700, Christoph Konrad wrote:
> Hello again,
>
> I have a further question with regards to groups within f(). Is it
> possible to have more than one group-level, ie something like 1|
> year:region:type? ("type" and "region" are categorical variables)

You have to do this manually, ie map "type" and "region" into a new
variable. INLA does not understand the 1|a:b:c syntax.

Best

H
